memo.verdict: Progress, not park. Neutral on the shares at SEK 390 (22 September 2026) and bullish below about SEK 360, the price at which the modal path clears the framework's 20 percent a year bar at the blended multiple (25 percent a year over eighteen months, 20 percent over three years); with no re-rating at all the bar is cleared at about SEK 340. Conviction medium: a working hypothesis on the earnings path, with the recurring base well evidenced and the multiple the open question. The gate does not close: no D or F sits on management (No mediocre management B), business quality (Business Element A), predictability (Transmission A) or trackability (Leading indicators A). The case is an 'OSHQC CfC Clearing' case rated B on fit, compelling on substance and not yet on price; the 'Investment Thesis' is a C at SEK 390 and would be a B below about SEK 360. First things to watch: the Q3 statement on 16 October 2026 and the August and September monthly statistics, for net inflow, the foreign share of turnover, net interest income above SEK 430 million a quarter and costs against the 9 percent guidance.
case: Avanza is a top-decile Swedish savings franchise whose transient, mostly external causes for concern have cleared before its multiple has. At SEK 390 the shares pay about 14 percent a year for that without any re-rating and about 18 percent a year with a less-than-even chance of one, against a 20 percent bar; the case is compelling on substance and not yet on price, and clears the bar only below about SEK 360.

The external change has turned from a two-year headwind into tailwinds. Three things de-rated the stock from about 22 times earnings to 17.6 times between 2024 and early 2026: the Riksbank's cuts from 4.0 percent to 1.75 percent through 2025 compressing net interest income; the supervisor's late-2024 deposit rules forcing the wind-down of the external Sparkonto+ product (a SEK 9 billion outflow in Q4 2024, the largest quarterly contraction in the platform's history); and the threat of an EU ban on fund commissions, 17 percent of 2025 income (Swedish fund commissions 60 percent of that). Each has cleared or paused: the Riksbank held in Q2 2026 and the STIBOR forward curve moved up about 20 basis points after the quarter; the wind-down completed on 13 May 2026 with 60 percent of the money retained on Avanza's own balance sheet at roughly ten times the spread (about 50 basis points against about 5; SEK 42 billion left external accounts since January 2025); the EU Retail Investment Strategy agreement of December 2025 introduced no general ban and the Swedish FSA announced it will not investigate a local one, though it still intends to study the feasibility of domestic rules. On top, the tax-free threshold on investment savings accounts doubled to SEK 300,000 in January 2026. The one new tax headwind is the loss of deductibility on margin-lending interest inside endowment insurance from 1 January 2026 (margin lending SEK 12.9 billion of a SEK 34 billion book), small. 'External forces' B: demand a cyclical, sector-level tailwind; competition tightening (Nordnet); disruption being disproved domestically; political and regulatory a tailwind; supply neutral; the company's own cycle turning up on all three engines at once; macro neutral. Not A because the strongest force, retail re-risking, is cyclical with less than two years' visibility, and the peer that matters is pulling away.

Retail risk appetite is both the strongest force and the cyclical top. Q2 2026 brought record net fund purchases of SEK 17 billion, total net inflow SEK 18.9 billion, foreign trading at 28 percent of turnover and currency income up 72 percent to SEK 224 million; transaction-related income was 44 percent of Q1 2026 income, summer months typically cut trading 13 percent month on month, and turnover per customer at Q2 levels is what DNB Carnegie calls a further 10 percent upside if extrapolated. The structural floor: Swedish household saving rates of 8 to 12 percent against 6 to 7 percent in the euro area; 44 percent of Nordic household financial assets in equities and funds against 30 percent in the EU; investment savings accounts at 29.8 percent of GDP. The "false friend" reading (customer growth masking falling assets per customer) is refuted: savings capital +22 percent on customers +8 percent. Competition C: Nordnet's savings capital rose 29 percent to SEK 1,374 billion against Avanza's 22 percent to 1,208 billion, Nordnet added 73,600 net customers in Q2 2026 (13 percent growth) against Avanza's 40,300 (8 percent); pricing is at parity (commission-free trading up to SEK 50,000 for new customers), no price war, the incumbent banks ineffective; Avanza's home share still rises (8.4 percent). Macro C: a parallel 1 point cut takes SEK 420 million off full-year net interest income (about 23 percent of consensus FY2026 net interest income and about 12 percent of consensus FY2026 pre-tax profit), a 1 point rise adds SEK 1,170 million; the sensitivity is asymmetric in the company's favour from 1.75 percent.
counter_case: At the head of the 'Investment Thesis': Avanza is a quality trap at a cyclical earnings peak. Transaction-related income was 44 percent of Q1 2026 revenue and Q2 delivered record fund purchases of SEK 17 billion, foreign trading at 28 percent of turnover and currency income up 72 percent; those are the marks of a top, not a base. Net interest income is at a record only because the Riksbank paused at 1.75 percent, and each further point of cuts takes SEK 420 million off it, with Swedish inflation near 0 to 0.5 percent in late 2026 arguing for cuts and the Riksbank calling its own path highly volatile. Costs are guided up 9 percent in 2026 and rise 11 to 12 percent in 2027 with Denmark, a venture Jefferies calls a bigger chance on a smaller prize against an incumbent, Nordnet, with 7 percent of Danish assets and the price-setter's seat, and for which Jefferies counts SEK 340 to 380 million over three years against the company's SEK 120 to 150 million plus running cost. The growth engine at home is structurally slower than the peer's (customers +8 percent against Nordnet's +13; savings capital +22 percent against +29), penetration is already 21 percent of the population, 2025's growth of 13 percent missed the company's own 15 percent target, and the market has said which it prefers: Nordnet +28.1 percent over twelve months against Avanza +17.6. So consensus growth of 6 to 7 percent a year for FY2027 and FY2028 is right, and the multiple belongs at the peer median of 15.3 times, which on consensus FY2027 earnings of SEK 20.58 is SEK 315, 19 percent below the price. Jefferies (Underperform, SEK 335) and Morgan Stanley (Underweight) hold versions of this view. On the record's own path the peer median returns 4 percent a year over eighteen months and 10 percent over three, an F and a D.

At the 'Foundations': Avanza's advantages are national and Nordnet's are regional, and in a business where scale on one platform lowers unit cost each period, the regional player wins the decade; Avanza's cost gap to Nordnet has already narrowed on DNB Carnegie's reading, and its answer, a second platform for one small market, adds cost without regional scale. Add a supervisor with a record of tightening (the deposit rules; a SEK 15 million data-protection fine) and a possible national commission study, and the foundation is a strong domestic franchise whose next growth leg is unproven and whose fee pool is regulator-dependent.
triggers: Price: the case clears the 20 percent bar below about SEK 360 at the blended multiple, and below about SEK 340 with no re-rating; the 'Investment Thesis' would be B and Headline Rating 4 B below about SEK 360.

The five things the case turns on, with what would change the view: savings capital compounding at about 11 percent a year (probable, about 65 percent; changed by monthly net inflow below 8 percent of capital a year for two quarters, or the market share turning down); the Riksbank holding at or near 1.75 percent through 2027 so the net-interest-income base holds within SEK 200 million (probable, about 60 percent; a quarter- or half-point cut plausible at about 40 percent, a full point unlikely at about 15 percent; changed by three-month STIBOR below 1.25 percent); transactional revenue normalising rather than collapsing, brokerage and currency income flat to 5 percent higher in 2027 (probable, about 60 percent; a 20 percent fall possible at about 25 percent; changed by a Swedish equity drawdown of 20 percent with monthly turnover down 30 percent); cost discipline holding at 9 percent in 2026, about 8 percent after, Denmark within SEK 150 million pre-launch and SEK 140 million a year after (probable, about 70 percent; changed by cost-to-savings above 15 basis points or a Danish budget above SEK 200 million); the multiple re-rating from 17.6 to 20 times by March 2028 (45 percent; changed either way by Nordnet's multiple, which sets the ceiling; below 17 times for Nordnet the re-rating leg is dead).

Invalidate levels: net inflow below 5 percent of capital a year for two quarters; net interest income below SEK 400 million in a quarter; a sequential operating margin below 50 percent; a Danish pre-launch budget above SEK 200 million. Alarm levels: net inflow below 8 percent a year; customer growth below 6 percent a year; foreign share of turnover below 22 percent; net interest income below SEK 430 million a quarter; STIBOR below 1.25 percent; cost growth above 10 percent for 2026 or cost-to-savings above 15 basis points; Danish pre-launch spend above SEK 150 million or mid-2028 without visible acceleration; operating margin below 60 percent; the multiple below 15.9 times with earnings unchanged, or Nordnet below 17 times; a consensus cut of 2 percent or more on any year. The re-rating leg is confirmed above 20 times.

Dated steps: the August and September 2026 monthly statistics; the Q3 statement on 16 October 2026, the first with a full quarter of the internalised deposits, watched for net inflow, the foreign share, net interest income above SEK 430 million and costs against 9 percent; H2 2026 cost delivery and the SEK 47 million of Danish spend; the Danish branch manager appointment; the wider Sigma roll-out; any Riksbank decision; the FY2026 result and dividend (consensus SEK 14.60; DNB Carnegie 15.20) in January to April 2027; the Ministry of Finance's answer on the free right to transfer occupational pensions; the Danish launch in H2 2027 with the first customer numbers; the 2027 STIBOR path against 2.25 percent; the margin-lending tax lobbying; Danish numbers through 2028 with mid-2028 as the point at which the launch must be visibly accelerating acquisition; Sigma at SEK 5 to 10 billion by 2028; a possible second European market.

Open items in the record itself: the earnings-momentum pin was absent on 22 September 2026 (the record's own reading would be B) and the peers' technical pins and three of their earnings pins are absent; no live thematics file, track-record file or Wisdom Library file was among the inputs, so 'Live thematics', 'Own errors' and 'Archetypes' are answered from the research only and 'Own errors' is provisional; the FactSet financials block carries the extractor's warning that its brokers'-basis actuals do not reconcile with its fundamentals history (revenue SEK 4,495 million against 5,737 million for FY2025), so completed-year figures are taken from the company's reported results; the AT1 coupon is the one earnings leakage the record could not size; the peers' multiple trend over recent months is not in the data; the FSA still intends to study the feasibility of domestic inducement rules, so the commission-ban risk is paused, not dead; the automated cash-sweeping disruption is named and untested; the dual platform will be judged by 2028.

judgement.heading: Avanza | Core Investment | 0.50% of the fund's capital in 1 tranche
judgement.markdown:
- **Industry:** G. Financials. Industry RS 73 at the Friday 2 October reading (86 four weeks earlier; 92 at the end of June)
- **Sector:** G.5. Online savings platform (direct to consumer). Sector RS 65 at the 30 September month-end (73 four weeks earlier; 62 on Monday's daily reading). Its other companies: Nordnet (Stock RS 71), AJ Bell (61), Fineco (52), Quilter (30), Flatex (9)
- **Cohort:** online investment and savings platforms (Nordic and European). The cohort's relative strength 61 (69 four weeks earlier), 4 companies: Nordnet (71), Fineco (52), Flatex (9)


**What is going on, and why it matters**

- **The price move by beta:** over 5 sessions the stock rose 2.6%; the market's fall explains -0.7%, so its own move was +3.3%, about its usual size (3.2%). Over 20 sessions it fell 1.2%, an own move of +1.1%, a fifth of its usual size.
  - A quiet stock at SEK 389.3, back where the memo was written (SEK 390 on 22 September)
- **The September statistics, published on Monday 5 October:** net inflow SEK 7.18 billion (SEK 7.35 billion in August, SEK 4.82 billion a year earlier; SEK 58.5 billion in the year to date); 19,200 new customers, 2.39 million in all; savings capital SEK 1.28 trillion, up 21% on the year
  - Daily brokerage notes 151,200, down 9% on the month and 11% on the year; foreign trading SEK 1.56 billion, down 10% on the month. <u>The flow side passes the memo's confirm level (above SEK 4 billion a month) comfortably; the activity side is softening, which is the counter-case's ground</u>
- **The sector and cohort:** the whole sector's relative strength is fading (Sector RS 65 from 84 at the end of August; the cohort 61 from 69). Within it the market still prefers Nordnet (Stock RS 71) to Avanza (56 at the month-end, 62 on Monday). The memo's own observation that this sector pays for growth over quality still holds
- **The analysts:** Net Upgrade Breadth, sales estimates +22% (18 analysts: 4 raised, none cut) and target prices +24% (21 analysts: 5 raised, none cut); Sell-side Momentum A. No analyst has cut in the last 100 days
- **The rule's reading that matters:** the 200-day average of relative price changed by +0.016% over the month at Friday's reading, against a trigger of zero or below; it read -0.1% the week before and fired. Monday's unofficial daily reading was +0.05%. The Friday 9 October reading decides whether it fires again.
  - On two sessions' evidence the odds of a re-fire are below even, perhaps one in three, because Monday's daily reading sits a little further from zero than Friday's; a week in which Avanza lags the market would reverse that

**What it means for the position**

- **Holding:** hold; none of the six Sell Criteria is met, and the bottom-up ratings (B on all four) are joint best in the book with Helios Towers
- **Selling:** the nearest fixed trigger is the relative 52W high trigger at about SEK 309, about 21% below, read on 30 October; the 30% level is SEK 285.81, 27% below; a sale on either is *unlikely this quarter*. The live risk is the slope criterion re-firing on Friday, *plausible within weeks*
  - If it fires and the one-off link no longer applies, the rule puts the whole holding on the 13 October order sheet, where you can overrule it with a recorded reason
- **Adding:** allowed by the rule (6.18% of room, 3.7 tranches of 1.67%; the next add takes Financials to 2.17% of capital); wanted, in steps. Four reasons for steps rather than one purchase: every top-down reading has moved towards its trigger for two months (section 3); the memo is neutral at SEK 390 and bullish only below about SEK 360
  - The slope criterion cleared by 0.016 points; and the third-quarter statement is on 16 October, ten days away, the first with a full quarter of the internalised deposits. Why a tranche now rather than waiting for SEK 360: the memo's verdict is progress, not park; no analyst has cut; September's inflows passed the confirm level
    - And at SEK 389 the modal return is still about 18% a year at the blended multiple, a C and close to our bar. One tranche at a C while the dated tests settle the rest is the trade-off I recommend; your intent is full size, and section 5 prices the three paths

**What we could lose:** about 0.10% of the fund's capital today, to the relative 52W high trigger; each new tranche of 1.67% adds about 0.34% to that figure (0.50% to its own 30% level, which starts 30% below its purchase price); at full size (6.68% of capital) about 1.37%

**Experiment: which stocks Avanza's own moves have tracked** (last 3 and 6 months)

- **Nordnet** (same sector, cohort and country of listing): 0.60 and 0.70, strong
- **Creades** (same country of listing; it holds about 10% of Avanza): 0.46 and 0.30, moderate
- **Flatex** (same sector and cohort): 0.32 and 0.41, moderate
- **AJ Bell** (same sector): 0.47 and 0.27, moderate
- **My reading:** look at Nordnet first; the pair move together

**The Investment Analyst's memo (digest of 22 September at SEK 390; memo republished 1 October)**

- **Decided:** progress, not park; neutral on the shares at SEK 390 and bullish below about SEK 360, the price at which the modal path clears 20% a year at the blended multiple; with no re-rating the bar is cleared at about SEK 340; conviction medium. The gate does not close: management B, business quality A, predictability A, trackability A
- **Must happen:** savings capital compounding at about 11% a year (a 7% market plus 4% to 5% net inflow); net interest income above SEK 430 million a quarter; costs within the 9% guidance; and for the full return, the multiple re-rating from 17.6 times towards 20 times (45% odds)
- **Main risk:** a quality trap at a cyclical earnings peak: transaction income was 44% of first-quarter revenue, each point of Riksbank cuts takes SEK 420 million off net interest income, and Nordnet compounds faster
- **Expected return (the Modal return):** about 18.4% a year over eighteen months at the blended multiple (13.9% with no re-rating) and 16.5% a year over three years, against our 20% a year bar: a C
- **Next test:** the third-quarter statement on 16 October (net inflow, the foreign share of turnover, net interest income above SEK 430 million, costs against 9%)

**My judgement:** bullish on the position, medium conviction: a top-decile business with no analyst cuts and inflows above the memo's confirm level, at the memo's neutral price; worth building to full size over four sessions, not one, because the top-down readings point the wrong way and the slope criterion could re-fire on Friday and stop every further add.

- **Counter-case:** the market is right to pay for Nordnet's growth over Avanza's quality; September's activity figures (brokerage notes down 9% on the month, 11% on the year) are the first sign the transaction peak is passing; relative strength falling for two months on every measure is the market saying so
  - And at SEK 389 the case pays about 14% a year without a re-rating, below our bar, so the better entry is SEK 360 or lower

**What would change my view:** the Friday 9 October slope reading (a fire means no further adds and a sale line on 13 October unless overruled); the 16 October statement (net interest income above SEK 430 million, net inflow, costs); a price below SEK 360, bullish on the memo's own terms

- The 30 October Stock RS reading (below 50, with the analysts turning to net cuts, would meet the fourth criterion; from today's counts, 4 raised and none cut of 18, that would take several cuts)
